heading: Major reportedly shot on parade by a soldier seeking discharge
finding: 1818 James Hamilton first said to have killed himself after shooting Major Birdsall; later update said Hamilton was in custody.
assessment: Both claims reproduced in later transcription of the Susquehanna Democrat, 31 July; original scan not yet checked.

heading: Newspaper admits publishing the forged “Roorback” election story
finding: 1844 political Roorback narrative circulated as genuine and was later acknowledged as fabricated.
assessment: Original fabrication issue B; locate exact original retraction before claiming issue-by-issue wording.

heading: First assassination telegram misstates the fate of Secretary Seward
finding: April 1865 newspapers falsely reported Secretary William Seward killed during assassination attack; he survived.
assessment: At least several precise Detroit/Memphis/Alabama issue leads, but original pages not systematically read.

heading: Judge calls a damaging Garfield campaign letter a forgery
finding: 1880 Morey/Garfield letter was printed as genuine by some outlets and later retracted as forged.
assessment: Allegations of authorship, motive and responsibility cannot be inferred from press endorsement/retraction.

heading: San Francisco “plague discovery” printed before the documented 1900 outbreak
finding: 1898 'plague discovered in San Francisco' newspaper rumor vs contemporaneous federal finding of no evidence.
assessment: Federal Public Health Reports is a primary correction, but not a second newspaper article; keep separate from 1900 plague.

heading: Gunness death disputed; an innocent traveler detained as supposed fugitive
finding: 1908 claimed arrest of Belle Gunness in Syracuse was corrected: detainee identified as Belle Herron.
assessment: New Haven Union 9 May source directly identifies mistaken arrest; separate body-identification dispute not yet reconciled.

heading: First Titanic sinking reports contradict each other on survivors and deaths
finding: Titanic early reports suggested rescued/saved passengers; 16 April Roseburg Review printed 866 survivors.
assessment: HN-382 and HN-383 are one sinking at successive reporting stages; survivor and lifeboat claims need timestamping.

heading: Newspaper updates Titanic toll but repeats false lifeboat assurances
finding: Titanic Carpathia arrival, survivor lists and lifeboat updates contradicted early optimistic bulletins.
assessment: Continuation of HN-382, not a second sinking.

heading: Lusitania sinking triggers conflicting first estimates and diplomatic alarms
finding: Lusitania May 1915 early reports included passengers saved or ship beached; later bulletins confirmed sinking and loss.
assessment: Timaru Herald 10 May prints sequential contradictory dispatches within one article.

heading: Wall Street blast initially mistaken for possible vehicle accident
finding: 1920 Wall Street explosion first-day Bend Bulletin: 16 killed and possible collision/accident or bomb.
assessment: Same incident as HN-424; first-day investigation remained open.

heading: Wall Street coverage revises the toll and identifies a bomb
finding: 17 September Albany Daily Democrat: bomb conclusion attributed to investigator, 36 dead and ~200 hurt.
assessment: Later phase of HN-423, not distinct attack; cause attributed to contemporary investigator.

heading: Attica hostage deaths: shots, not knives
finding: Attica 1971 first attributed hostage deaths to knives; autopsies disclosed hostages had been shot.
assessment: Manchester Evening Herald 15 Sept and Notre Dame Observer 20 Sept A documented reversal; early knife attribution still needs exact issue.

heading: Armero toll feared near 20,000 amid dangerous rescue efforts
finding: Armero LA Times 15 Nov 1985 appended 16 Nov correction to the name of a Colombian newspaper.
assessment: A published editorial correction, not a second death figure; death estimates remained fluid.

heading: Loma Prieta quake initially blamed for at least 271 deaths
finding: Loma Prieta quake: Los Angeles Times 18 Oct 1989 ran headline 273 killed; Washington Post 26 Oct reconstructed Lieutenant Governor's 271 estimate as inflated.
assessment: HN-781 covers freeway-specific downward correction; do not mix total quake deaths with freeway subset.

heading: Earthquake death estimates retreat as California recovers
finding: Loma Prieta: Los Angeles Times 20 Oct sharply lowered Nimitz freeway deaths; Washington Post 26 Oct analyzed the erroneous early tallies.
assessment: A different stage of HN-780, not a second quake.

heading: Newspaper describes FBI's false Madrid fingerprint identification
finding: FBI's Madrid 2004 fingerprint match tied Brandon Mayfield to attack; Spain questioned it and FBI later withdrew identification.
assessment: LA Times May 26 and Washington Post May 25 document correction; June Indiana story later.

heading: Rosa Parks's death prompts reflection on the choice to resist
finding: Washington Post 25 Oct 2005 obituary of Rosa Parks carries a published correction about the name of an honor.
assessment: Verify exact correction text in publisher item; no independent conflicting press quotation yet.

heading: Student column misidentifies North Korea's underground nuclear test
finding: North Korea October 2006 nuclear-test claim initially unconfirmed by initial reports; Washington Post 16 October published radioactive-air-sample confirmation.
assessment: Do not infer unspecified error in November Indiana student column.

heading: Paradise's Camp Fire: nine initially reported dead
finding: Camp Fire on 9 November 2018 San Francisco Chronicle 'at least five dead' vs LA Times same day 'at least nine dead'.
assessment: Successive same-day updates, not two final figures.

heading: Scholar advances an answer to Westminster Abbey sarcophagus mystery
finding: Westminster Abbey Roman sarcophagus: medieval occupant proposed as Ã†lfwig rather than Wulfnoth; identification remains hypothesis.
assessment: Competing candidate interpretations, not two confirmed identifications.

heading: A newspaper challenges the evidence for the Somers hangings
finding: 1843 press argued opposite positions about the USS Somers commander's conduct and quality of evidence.
assessment: Editorial disagreement, not an independently settled verdict.

heading: Steamship Tioga blast: rival boiler and cargo theories
finding: 1890 Tioga steamer explosion attributed alternatively to a boiler failure and dangerous cargo.
assessment: Competing preliminary causal hypotheses, not proven explanations.

heading: Frank Slide blamed on “mine damp”; later geologists identify mountain instability
finding: 1903 Frank Slide contemporaries debated eruption/volcano, mine damp and other mechanisms while toll changed.
assessment: These were hypotheses; a same-date Oregon rockfall story is a DIFFERENT incident, explicitly excluded.

heading: Labor newspaper describes deadly attack on Ludlow tent colony
finding: Ludlow 1914 miners and militia blamed one another for deaths and tent-colony destruction.
assessment: Attribution dispute; early sensational totals not verified.

heading: Maddox confrontation portrayed as an unprovoked attack
finding: Gulf of Tonkin 2 August 1964 USS Maddox engagement is distinct from disputed 4 August claimed second attack.
assessment: Do not treat the later disputed encounter as established by reporting on the first.

heading: Mexico City violence raises fears for Olympic Games
finding: Tlatelolco October 1968 news headlines differ over military response, snipers, responsibility and casualties.
assessment: 11 newspaper headline leads all B; full article-level attribution and toll extraction remain unperformed.

heading: Beslan school massacre triggers a dispute over language in headlines
finding: 2004 Beslan reporting contested labeling assailants 'militants' vs 'terrorists' and use of images/headlines.
assessment: Guardian readers' editor 11 Sept documents wording dispute; Indiana's exact wording untranscribed.

heading: Ferguson reporting explicitly repeats a rumored quotation
finding: Ferguson witness words and 'hands up' account disputed by competing witnesses and subsequent evidence.
assessment: Guardian Sept2014 A discusses testimony; do not invent the student's purported exact quote.

heading: Russia–Turkey–ISIS oil allegations remain conditional in newspaper debate
finding: Dec2015 Russia claimed Turkish leadership benefited from ISIS oil; Turkey denied and traded counter-accusations; US officials skeptical.
assessment: Washington Post and LA Times same-day A; accusation not established.

heading: Mahsa Amini's death sparks protest amid disputed police account
finding: Mahsa Amini 2022 family challenged Iranian authorities' explanation of death after morality-police detention.
assessment: Washington Post Sept16 A contains rival accounts; LA Times Sept22 covers later protest phase.

heading: Haitian military leaders address reports of killings during revolt
finding: 13 January 1804 LOC seed versus 12 January bibliography citation; publication/issue identification unresolved.
assessment: Bibliographic date mismatch, NOT proven competing article content.

heading: Liverpool church tower falls through the building before services
finding: Liverpool St Nicholas collapse: 11 February 1810 vs January in a later transcription.
assessment: Later transcription error candidate; Liverpool Saturday Advertiser 17 February is an unread issue lead.

heading: US Supreme Court temporarily blocks a transgender-prisoner care restriction
finding: 21 October 2026 Supreme Court rejected emergency stay; some phrasing 'blocks ban' may overstate legal finality.
assessment: Procedural outcome only, no merits ruling; compare article headlines with order.

heading: Iran warns of attacks on Gulf oil and AI facilities if war resumes
finding: Iranian conditional threat to Gulf digital/oil assets was reported by 13 and 19 October, before 22 October seed; target lists evolved.
assessment: Continuing public threat, not fresh attack or wholly new warning.

heading: Steamboat Benjamin Franklin boiler explosion at Mobile
finding: The steamboat Benjamin Franklin explosion is associated with conflicting incident dates.
assessment: Read original 1836 newspaper issue and distinguish dateline, event date and publication date.

heading: New steamboat Medora explodes on a Chesapeake trial run
finding: Medora explosion seed dated 29 April 1842, yet putative Baltimore American victim obituaries are 15–16 April.
assessment: Impossible chronology if same disaster; article identity/date unverified. Could be seed date or different event.

heading: Collision blamed for Empire State steamboat explosion
finding: 1853 New York Herald calls wrecked steamer Empire, but student seed says Empire State.
assessment: May be name variation OR another vessel; do not equate yet.

heading: Poisoning allegation challenges first account of Arctic explorer's death
finding: 1873 New York Herald 'Story of Ice' citation gives page 5 in one record and page 12 in another.
assessment: Pagination/catalog inconsistency, not historical claim disagreement.

heading: Cleveland powder mills destroyed in a series of blasts
finding: Austin powder works explosion is 16 March 1875; linked Brooklyn Eagle citation says 17 March 1874, with separate 1872 explosion.
assessment: Potentially mistaken article identity. Held from same-event source count.

heading: Headline overstates Nazi mass-arrest count
finding: Kristallnacht Indiana seed carried 50,000 arrests; contemporary Northern Advocate and Bend Bulletin did not corroborate that number.
assessment: ~30,000 from later USHMM is a retrospective comparison, not second contemporaneous figure.

heading: Capitol shooting report miscounts attackers
finding: 1954 Capitol shooting some seed/newspaper headlines say THREE attackers, but FOUR participated.
assessment: New York Times 2 March reproduced-headline B; five wounded legislators is a separate count.

heading: Integrated Montgomery bus service faces sniper violence
finding: 1956 Rosa Jordan bus shooting collector title says 'shot dead'; actual report describes a woman wounded while pregnant.
assessment: Seed/collector-label error; do not add to fatality events.

heading: Student aviation-safety report gets Flight 800's crash date wrong
finding: TWA Flight 800 crashed evening 17 July 1996; Indiana student tracker identifies an erroneous date.
assessment: LA Times and Washington Post independently confirm 17 July. Student paper's exact erroneous numeral still untranscribed.

heading: Hurricane Mitch damages Honduras's only reported synagogue
finding: Hurricane Mitch paper/seed suggests Honduras's 'only synagogue' destroyed; same contemporaneous Jewish Week article says San Pedro Sula synagogue was undamaged.
assessment: Internal claim conflict: Tegucigalpa site damaged, at least one separate intact synagogue documented.

heading: Student newspaper documents Columbine's thirteen victims
finding: Columbine 1999 13 murdered people (12 students and one teacher), plus two perpetrators; 15 killed INCLUDING perpetrators.
assessment: Inclusion-rule issue, not 15 victims. Two retrospective-period A articles document count.

heading: Haiti-earthquake story prints the wrong calendar year
finding: Haiti quake on 12 January 2010, not 2009 as flagged in tracker.
assessment: Actual numeral in seed issue needs transcription; two independent Jan2010 articles corroborate event date.

heading: Student report captures East Palestine's early technical theory
finding: East Palestine early February 2023 overheating wheel-bearing hypothesis vs need for definitive investigation; HN-991/992 cover one derailment.
assessment: Do not substitute preliminary theory for final established cause. B seed exact prose uninspected.
taxonomy_leaf: Train derailments and hazardous freight incidents

heading: Mammoth mine disaster: shifting counts and a later federal correction
finding: 1891 Mammoth mine: Evening Capital Journal 28 January says 107 bodies recovered; later histories cite 109 deaths.
assessment: Different dates and measures; must not label 107 versus 109 a contemporaneous falsehood.

heading: Tri-State Tornado early reports exceed 1,000 deaths
finding: Tri-State tornado 1925 seed reported feared over 1,000 casualties; later histories use 695 dead.
assessment: Early 'casualties' is not necessarily deaths, and later figure is retrospective.

heading: New London school-explosion toll climbs
finding: New London 1937 school blast: Texas Daily News-Telegram 19 March and NZ Northern Advocate 20 March both printed 500 deaths.
assessment: Those two A papers AGREE on an inflated preliminary claim; not evidence of cross-paper conflict; seek later corrections.

heading: Winecoff Hotel blaze reported with an inflated first death toll
finding: Winecoff fire Medford Mail Tribune 8 December 1946 says 122 deaths; later standard figure is 119.
assessment: Newspaper-to-retrospective revision; obtain a second contemporaneous final correction.

heading: Good Friday Alaska earthquake produces fires and tidal waves
finding: 1964 Alaska earthquake first days feared 500–600 deaths; later official toll much lower.
assessment: One A packet; later figure retrospective. Not contemporaneous disagreement established.

heading: Armenian earthquake relief begins amid fears of tens of thousands dead
finding: Armenia 1988 quake Los Angeles Times 9 Dec feared losses could reach 100,000, while Washington Post said tens of thousands.
assessment: Forecast fear vs rounded estimate; not a stable confirmed count contradiction.

heading: El Paso: early Walmart shooting toll was provisional
finding: El Paso Aug2019 first reports 20 dead and 26 injured; subsequent death tally increased.
assessment: Only early-stage 20 sourced in current packet; later dated article required for documented numeric comparison.

heading: Beirut port explosion: 78 deaths was an initial count
finding: Beirut 2020 initial seed 78 fatalities while Washington Post described 'more than 70' and >3,000 injured.
assessment: 78 satisfies >70; these are compatible early figures, not evidence of contradiction.

heading: Distant report claims a thousand killed by lightning-triggered magazine blast
finding: 1857 powder-magazine catastrophe indexed with inconsistent 'Rondpore'/Persia geographic descriptions and >1,000 dead.
assessment: Index-derived; obtain Tipton Advertiser 19 December page text.

heading: Clerkenwell Prison blast and uncertain early arrests
finding: Clerkenwell explosion December 1867 first-day dispatches published different fatality figures.
assessment: Manchester Guardian 14 December read; extract comparable numbers from another dated paper.

heading: Senator Chandler found dead after a campaign speech; medical explanations differ
finding: Reports on Senator Zachariah Chandler's 1879 death conflict in medical explanations; secondary index misplaces Detroit hotel.
assessment: Needs exact primary death report and source-by-source comparison.

heading: Vienna Ringtheater fire: initial estimates exceed later official minimum
finding: Vienna Ringtheater fire was 8 December 1881; 16 December is seed publication. Provisional deaths differed widely.
assessment: Numbers have not been transcribed across every held newspaper issue.

heading: Frontenac mine toll first inflated, then sharply revised
finding: Frontenac coal mine 1888 original wire supposedly asserted 90 bodies recovered; later accounting cites 44 dead.
assessment: 90 is an issue-index claim (B), not article text checked; recovered-vs-dead measures may differ.

heading: Bank robber extorts $21,000 with a pistol and fake explosive
finding: 1889 Denver Moffat bank extortion dispatches differ on precise event day and alleged offender identity.
assessment: Earlier and later A reports; check exact lines before drawing firm conclusion.

heading: Coal-mine death count rises at Braznell, Pennsylvania
finding: 1899 Braznell mine explosion's early fatality estimates were greatly overstated/variable.
assessment: Specific side-by-side numbers still missing from original A pages.

heading: Galveston newspaper count falls far below the catastrophe's later scale
finding: 1900 Galveston hurricane papers printed lower and higher preliminary death tolls even on 14 September.
assessment: Five A appearances saved; numerators need extracting from each original page.

heading: Vladivostok mutiny rumors outpace verified casualty information
finding: 1905 Vladivostok mutiny foreign wires gave competing accounts of severity, fire and loss of life.
assessment: Seven newspaper pages linked, figures not normalized by original dispatch timestamp.

heading: San Francisco quake coverage swings toward 5,000 estimated dead
finding: 1906 San Francisco earthquake seed printed an estimate toward 5,000 dead.
assessment: Four A follow-ups with incomplete figures; do not equate this seed estimate with verified deaths.

heading: Messina earthquake news mixes confirmed destruction with exaggerated geography
finding: 1908 Messina earthquake first papers differ in quake geography and provisional casualties.
assessment: Six original dated pages; extract their literal casualty counts and dateline before adjudicating.

heading: Burning liner Morro Castle wrecked off New Jersey
finding: 1934 Morro Castle first-day dispatches gave different dead, missing and rescued numbers.
assessment: La Grande Evening Observer's own issue has multiple numbers; B dealer/index sources need opening.

heading: Indira Gandhi assassination reported with a shifting account of assailants
finding: Indira Gandhi assassination 1984 first dispatches differ on number/status of bodyguard attackers.
assessment: Lawton Constitution 31 Oct and Washington Post 1 Nov read; exact variants not recorded.

heading: TWA hijacking enters a second day with changing hostage details
finding: TWA 847 hijack 1985 early number of hijackers, passengers, released hostages and deaths changed hourly.
assessment: Washington Post and Los Angeles Times 15 June A; no verbatim count matrix yet.

heading: Hurricane Trudy threatens Mexico as floods strike Greece
finding: 19 October 2026 Guardian wraps two independent events: Pacific Hurricane Trudy AND Greek/Rhodes storms; Rhodes victim described as 25 in a 14 Oct original but 62 in later indexed coverage.
assessment: Two separate event packets required; age mismatch unresolved because latter item not opened; do not conflate hurricane and Greek floods.

heading: Black Tom ammunition depot explodes near New York Harbor
finding: Black Tom 31 July 1916: Morning Oregonian THREE known dead and at least FIVE missing versus Eugene Daily Guard FOUR killed and ELEVEN–TWENTY missing.
assessment: Both primary issue OCRs checked this turn. Different dispatch dates/times; Eugene Guard additionally reports $25–45m property losses versus Oregonian $25m.

heading: Chicago officials pronounce riot ended as toll rises to 32
finding: Chicago 1919 violence: Indiana 1 August seed gives 32 dead; Eugene Daily Guard 1 August reports 34.
assessment: Same publication date, advancing toll; investigate wire datelines, not a proven deliberate misstatement.

heading: Tulsa attack reported as 'race riot' with nearly 100 dead
finding: Tulsa 1921 first coverage variously reported 56, 75, 80, and about 100 dead; some accounts blamed Black residents while describing destruction of Black neighborhoods.
assessment: 56/75/100 are LOC guide's specific headlines (B); County Record's 'Eighty Killed' is A. Severe sourcing/perspective discrepancy; do NOT treat as reliable final toll.

heading: Hartford tent-fire deaths revised to 153
finding: Hartford circus fire 8 July 1944: Indiana seed 153 dead vs Eugene Register-Guard same day 152; Oregon Statesman 9 July says 'over 150'.
assessment: 152 vs 153 directly comparable early tallies; 'over 150' is a range, not numeric contradiction.

heading: Atomic test targets a fleet at Bikini Atoll
finding: Bikini Able test 1 July 1946: seed '20 damaged'; Midland Reporter-Telegram says 3 sunk and 8 damaged; Wanganui Herald described largely undamaged-looking ships.
assessment: Counts are NOT necessarily same definitions or inspection time. Able must remain separate from 25 July Baker test.

heading: Texas City disaster proclaimed to have killed 700
finding: Texas City 17 April 1947: Medford Mail Tribune quotes Red Cross 714, governor 600–650 and ~400 bodies recovered; Pampa News 650; Cameron Herald 'may reach 700'.
assessment: Different official estimates and recovered-body measure; source/clock required. Grandcamp and later High Flyer explosions are sequential.

heading: Silver Bridge rescuers feared death toll could reach 80
finding: Silver Bridge December 1967: Point Pleasant Register 18 Dec lists 16 dead/44 missing; Charleston Gazette-Mail 17 Dec 8 dead/46 missing; Charleston Daily Mail 16 Dec 'may reach 46'.
assessment: All these exact headline leads B via WV archive; DIFFERENT reporting stages and dead/missing fields; needs page reads.

heading: Mexico City earthquake initially reported as 7.8, with 230 confirmed dead
finding: Mexico City quake 20 Sept 1985: Lawton Morning Press police count at least 170; seed ~230; Muskogee Daily Phoenix TV estimate at least 250.
assessment: Same disaster, different partial/dated source estimates. 'At least' lower bounds do not logically contradict larger totals.

heading: USS Stark death count revised upward from 28 to 37
finding: USS Stark 19 May 1987 Los Angeles Times and Muskogee Daily Phoenix: 28 dead; Washington Post 19 May dispatch/20 May archive: 37 dead or presumed dead.
assessment: A documented upward revision; 37 includes presumed dead, status difference matters.

heading: Pakistan earthquake article shows a rapidly rising death toll
finding: Pakistan earthquake October 2005: Guardian 20 Oct reports ~79,000 toll; LA Times 18 Oct distinguishes lower official tally and locally generated estimates.
assessment: Different dates/methods; no reason to call either a knowingly false final count.

heading: Sago families receive a false announcement of survival
finding: Sago mine January 2006: announcement that 12 miners were alive was false; papers corrected to 12 dead/one survivor. LA Times printed survivor's name 'Ronald McCloy'; Washington Post gives Randal McCloy.
assessment: Two separate inconsistencies: false rescue claim and wrong given name. Source-specific contemporary correction.

heading: H1N1 dispatch reports 403 U.S. cases and one death
finding: May 2009 H1N1 reporting: 403 confirmed US cases and second US death were both reported 4–5 May; seed 'one death' attached to same stage may be stale.
assessment: Verify seed wording/time to distinguish old count from real simultaneous inconsistency.

heading: Gulf oil-spill columnist uses a then-current flow estimate
finding: Deepwater Horizon 14 May 2010 Washington Post contrasts 5,000 vs 26,000 barrels/day; Los Angeles Times reports scientist's rate higher than government 5,000.
assessment: Contemporaneous methodological disagreement; both were preliminary, later estimates distinct.

heading: Early Pulse nightclub casualty reporting contains a counting trap
finding: Pulse June2016 early count '50 dead' versus later '49 victims' clarified that 50 includes attacker and 49 excludes him.
assessment: LA Times June12 vs Washington Post June12/13. Different denominators, not disappearance of a victim.
